prompt:
Research the officially documented limits of GitHub Pages (published site size, monthly bandwidth, builds per hour). Cite GitHub's documentation page and quote the limits.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Based on GitHub's official documentation, here are the key limits for GitHub Pages:

**Published Site Size:** GitHub Pages sites have a maximum published size of 1 GB.
SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/github-pages-limits | QUOTE: "Published GitHub Pages sites may be no larger than 1 GB." | CLAIM: The maximum size for a published GitHub Pages site is 1 GB.

**Monthly Bandwidth:** GitHub Pages sites have a soft bandwidth limit of 100 GB per month.
SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/github-pages-limits | QUOTE: "GitHub Pages sites have a soft bandwidth limit of 100 GB per month." | CLAIM: There is a soft monthly bandwidth limit of 100 GB.

**Builds per Hour:** GitHub Pages sites have a soft limit of 10 builds per hour when using the built-in Pages build process.
SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/github-pages-limits | QUOTE: "GitHub Pages sites have a soft limit of 10 builds per hour." | CLAIM: There is a soft limit of 10 builds per hour for the standard GitHub Pages build process.

It's important to note that this build limit does not apply if you publish your site using a custom GitHub Actions workflow.
